categories.title: Foundations of Quantum Mechanics
categories.summary: What does quantum theory say about reality, and why does the world have its particular quantum structure?
paragraphs: Quantum theory predicts interference and correlations with extraordinary precision. Its foundations ask what those predictions mean, which physical assumptions support them, and how the familiar world emerges from them.

The questions here distinguish mathematical consequences of the formalism, competing interpretations, and proposals with different experimental predictions. Begin with measurement for the tension within the theory, or correlations for a precise boundary between classical and quantum models.

children.title: Why does a measurement have one outcome?
children.keyword: Why does a measurement have one outcome?
children.summary: Unitary dynamics predicts an entangled system and apparatus. What connects that description to a definite recorded result?
paragraphs: Unitary dynamics predicts an entangled system and apparatus. What connects that description to a definite recorded result?

children.title: What does a state look like relative to an observer?
children.keyword: What does a state look like relative to an observer?
children.summary: Call one part of an entangled pair the observer. Each of its basis states then picks out a state of the other part. How do these relative states change with the observer’s basis, and when does that give the Schmidt form?
paragraphs: Call one part of an entangled pair the observer. Each of its basis states then picks out a state of the other part. How do these relative states change with the observer’s basis, and when does that give the Schmidt form?

children.title: Why are quantum correlations limited?
children.summary: Bell inequalities exclude local hidden-variable models, but no-signalling alone allows correlations stronger than quantum theory.
paragraphs: Bell inequalities exclude local hidden-variable models, but no-signalling alone allows correlations stronger than quantum theory.

children.title: How does a classical world emerge?
children.keyword: How does a classical world emerge?
children.summary: Loss of local interference is only part of the story: stable, independently accessible records must also be explained.
paragraphs: Loss of local interference is only part of the story: stable, independently accessible records must also be explained.

children.keyword: How can gravity and quantum theory be tested together?
children.summary: A branch-dependent gravitational phase offers a tractable starting point, but interpreting an entanglement signal requires explicit assumptions.
paragraphs: A branch-dependent gravitational phase offers a tractable starting point, but interpreting an entanglement signal requires explicit assumptions.

categories.title: Quantum Computation
categories.summary: Which problems can quantum systems solve efficiently, and what resources make that possible?
paragraphs: A computational advantage is a statement about a task, a family of inputs, an error tolerance, and a resource model. A large state space alone does not establish an advantage.
These questions connect computational complexity to physical simulation and error-corrected computation. They ask both what can be achieved in principle and what must be paid to achieve it.

children.title: What can quantum computers compute efficiently?
children.keyword: What can quantum computers compute efficiently?
children.summary: Interference produces remarkable algorithms, but the boundary of efficient quantum computation is still incompletely understood.
paragraphs: Interference produces remarkable algorithms, but the boundary of efficient quantum computation is still incompletely understood.

children.title: When does simulating quantum matter become useful?
children.keyword: When does simulating quantum matter become useful?
children.summary: Efficiently producing a quantum evolution is different from efficiently extracting a scientifically useful prediction.
paragraphs: Efficiently producing a quantum evolution is different from efficiently extracting a scientifically useful prediction.

children.title: What does reliable quantum computation cost?
children.keyword: What does reliable quantum computation cost?
children.summary: Error correction changes the scaling of failure, but practical overhead depends on codes, noise, gates, and architecture together.
paragraphs: Error correction changes the scaling of failure, but practical overhead depends on codes, noise, gates, and architecture together.

categories.title: Quantum Information
categories.summary: What can be transmitted, recovered, and transformed when information is encoded in quantum states?
paragraphs: Quantum information makes physical constraints into quantitative tasks. How many entangled pairs can two laboratories extract? How much unknown quantum information can a noisy channel transmit? Which correlations survive losing part of a system?
The same density matrix can support different operational questions. Each page states the allowed operations and resources before assigning an information quantity or a limit.

children.title: Is entanglement a reversible resource?
children.summary: Pure-state entanglement has a clean asymptotic currency. Mixed states reveal irreversibility and limits to that description.
paragraphs: Pure-state entanglement has a clean asymptotic currency. Mixed states reveal irreversibility and limits to that description.

children.title: How much quantum information can noise transmit?
children.keyword: How much quantum information can noise transmit?
children.summary: Quantum channel capacity requires both a coding strategy and a converse bound; optimizing one use is not generally enough.
paragraphs: Quantum channel capacity requires both a coding strategy and a converse bound; optimizing one use is not generally enough.

children.title: When is lost quantum information recoverable?
children.keyword: When is lost quantum information recoverable?
children.summary: Recovery depends on what the environment learned, not simply on whether a noisy transformation has an algebraic inverse.
paragraphs: Recovery depends on what the environment learned, not simply on whether a noisy transformation has an algebraic inverse.

categories.title: Quantum Technology
categories.summary: How can fragile quantum effects become reliable processors, networks, and measuring instruments?
paragraphs: An ideal protocol becomes a technology only when control, noise, measurement, and resource costs can be handled together. The important comparison is with a credible alternative under the same conditions.
These pages connect small mathematical models to measurable engineering requirements. Illustrative parameters explain a trade-off; they are not forecasts or rankings of current devices.

children.title: Can quantum devices remain controllable as they grow?
children.keyword: Can quantum devices remain controllable as they grow?
children.summary: A scalable device must preserve useful control and verifiable performance as calibration, connectivity, and correlated errors grow.
paragraphs: A scalable device must preserve useful control and verifiable performance as calibration, connectivity, and correlated errors grow.

children.title: Can quantum networks overcome distance and loss?
children.keyword: Can quantum networks overcome distance and loss?
children.summary: Repeaters promise a different rate–distance trade-off, but loss, memory, and scheduling must be accounted for together.
paragraphs: Repeaters promise a different rate–distance trade-off, but loss, memory, and scheduling must be accounted for together.
